questions.questionText: When did F.W. de Klerk begin reforms?
questions.explanation: De Klerk became president in 1989 and began unbanning organizations and releasing prisoners.

questions.questionText: What was CODESA?
questions.diagram: Convention for a Democratic South Africa.
questions.explanation: CODESA (1991-1993) brought together government and liberation movements to design transition.

questions.questionText: When was Nelson Mandela released?
questions.explanation: Mandela walked free from Pollsmoor Prison after 27 years of imprisonment, ending isolation.

questions.questionText: What was the Interim Constitution?

options.text: Constitution guaranteeing equal rights during transition

questions.explanation: The Interim Constitution (1993) established democratic principles, human rights, and transitional structures.

questions.questionText: What was the Negotiated Settlement?

options.text: Agreement between apartheid government and liberation movements

questions.explanation: Negotiators agreed to power-sharing, transitional government, and democratic elections.

questions.questionText: What was the Multi-Party Negotiation Process?
questions.explanation: Multi-party negotiations at World Trade Center produced constitutional agreements and Transitional Executive Council.

questions.questionText: What was the 1993 White Paper?

options.text: Outlined transition to democracy and election plans

questions.explanation: White Paper established detailed plans for democratic election, constitutional principles, and transition structures.

questions.questionText: What were the main challenges during negotiations?

options.text: Violence, power-sharing formulas, and白马 minority concerns

questions.explanation: Negotiators faced violence from right-wing and Inkatha, debates over federalism, and fear of retributive violence.

questions.questionText: How did the National Party approach negotiations?

options.text: Seeking power-sharing and protection for white minority

questions.explanation: National Party negotiated to maintain some power, secure constitutional protections, and avoid retribution.

questions.questionText: What role did international factors play in the transition?

options.text: Sanctions relief and international recognition incentivized change

questions.explanation: End of Cold War, continued sanctions, and international isolation made accommodation with apartheid untenable.

questions.questionText: What was the Transition Executive Council?

options.text: Body sharing power during transition period

questions.explanation: TEC allowed liberation movements to participate in governance before elections, sharing executive authority.

questions.questionText: How did violence affect negotiations?

options.text: Threatened to derail talks but ultimately strengthened resolve

questions.explanation: Mafia-backed, right-wing, and Inkatha violence attempted to derail negotiations but failed.

questions.questionText: What was the concern about 'sunset clauses'?

options.text: Guarantees protecting public servants and minority rights

questions.explanation: Sunset clauses protected civil service jobs and guaranteed power-sharing to reassure whites.

questions.questionText: What was the significance of the 1993 constitutional principles?

options.text: Established non-racial democracy and human rights framework

questions.explanation: 34 Principles guided final constitution, guaranteeing citizenship, rights, and democratic governance.

questions.questionText: Analyze the compromises made during negotiations.

options.text: Liberals accepted power-sharing, whites secured protections, all accepted democratic transition

questions.explanation: Liberation movements accepted power-sharing and minority guarantees; government accepted democratic majority rule.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the role of negotiation leaders in the transition.

options.text: Mandela and De Klerk's statesmanship enabled peaceful settlement
Leaders had no role in transition

questions.explanation: Mandela and De Klerk's willingness to negotiate, trust-building, and pragmatism made settlement possible.

questions.questionText: How did the negotiated settlement compare to other African transitions?

options.text: Unique peaceful settlement with power-sharing unprecedented in Africa

questions.explanation: South Africa's negotiated settlement was exceptional for its peaceful nature and power-sharing provisions.

questions.questionText: Analyze how fear of violence shaped negotiations.

options.text: Both sides wanted to avoid civil war, driving them to compromise
Violence had no effect on negotiations

questions.explanation: Threat of civil war, especially between ANC and Zulu, motivated all parties to reach agreement.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the legacy of the negotiated settlement for democracy.

options.text: Established precedent for inclusive, peaceful political change

questions.explanation: Settlement demonstrated that negotiated transitions are possible, influencing global conflict resolution.

questions.questionText: How did the media contribute to the transition?

options.text: Covered negotiations, exposed violence, and built public support for democracy

questions.explanation: Media reported on negotiations, exposed state violence, and educated public about democratic processes.
